correctness.rationale: The proof bounds total approvals of selected candidates by twice the number of voters outside a JR-witness group. The threshold forces a selected score tied at the quota, and maximal coverage removes the only equality obstruction by a second exchange. Balanced two-approval ballots give a unique welfare optimum violating JR whenever the reverse inequality holds. The two-seat and singleton-ballot statements have direct disjoint-support counting proofs. A standalone Python verifier independently checked 850,550 anonymous finite profiles and 100 explicit witness sizes; finite checks only corroborate the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: The original contribution is the exact all-populations phase condition for joint approval-welfare optimality and JR when each ballot approves at most two candidates, with four-candidate obstruction and minimality of three seats and two allowed approvals. The full accessible primary Price of Justified Representation manuscript treats welfare-JR tradeoffs generally, not this exact restricted-domain criterion. The 2026 core-existence paper proves fair committees exist but does not demand ordinary approval-welfare optimality. Targeted comparisons against primary publications and mathematically relevant indexed claims did not reveal equivalent or stronger coverage. Remaining risk is unindexed sparse-approval results, not an assertion of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently titled earlier results may prove equivalent zero-price-of-JR conditions for two-approval ballots.
Some recent related full texts are inaccessible or not fully examined; an abstract does not exclude stronger coverage.
Semantic search may fail to rank mathematically equivalent work; unsuccessful retrieval is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: The exact population/residue phase for a familiar natural welfare-vs-representation tradeoff is a meaningful mathematical classification: it identifies the sharp first obstruction at nine voters, compatibility restoration at ten and eleven, a general family of obstructions for every negative size, and the minimality of the approval and seat dimensions. This is not a textbook renaming or arbitrary finite computation; the result includes an all-n theorem and construction.
